reference.title: Suspended Row
reference.listing: Animated GIF (title from the catalog listing; the page could not be read from this environment, so the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as you row the bar to the stomach, breathe in as the arms straighten.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s pull, short squeeze, about 2 s return

prescription.load: Bodyweight; set the body angle so the last reps are hard with 1-3 reps in reserve (RIR 1-3, clinical opinion)
prescription.progression: Lower the body angle, then raise the feet

cues.text: Hold a handle in each hand, palms facing in; walk the feet forward and lean back until the arms are long, heels down, body straight from heels to head.
Breathe out and pull the chest up to the hands, elbows close to the body.
Squeeze the shoulder blades together; hips stay up in line with the body.
Breathe in and lower slowly until the arms are long again.
Keep the glutes and abs tight; repeat.

mistakes.fix: Squeeze the glutes and brace; the body stays in one line.

mistakes.mistake: Shrugging the shoulders up to the ears
mistakes.fix: Pull the shoulder blades back and down.
Keep the elbows close to the ribs for this row.
Lower over about 2 s to long arms.

kinematics.norm: The more upright the body, the easier the row; walking the feet forward toward the anchor makes it harder (clinical opinion)
From nearly straight to about 90-110 degrees at the top (clinical opinion)
Protracted with the arms long, retracted at the top; retraction work drives the middle trapezius and rhomboids (Oyama 2010)
Straps stay taut and close to vertical; the hands stay on the strap arcs about the anchor (geometry)
Controlled, about 1 s up and 2 s down (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #2290, Suspended Row, animated GIF (movement reference)
Fenwick, Brown & McGill 2009, comparison of different rowing exercises: trunk muscle activation and lumbar spine motion, load and stiffness (J Strength Cond Res 23(2):350-358)
Oyama, Myers, Wassinger and Lephart 2010, three-dimensional scapular and clavicular kinematics and scapular muscle activity during retraction exercises (J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 40(3):169-179)

cautions: Check the anchor and the straps before each set; anchor only to a sturdy bar or a door anchor made for it.
Shoulder pain: stand more upright and shorten the range (clinical opinion).
Keep the straps taut; do not let them rub on the arms.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Gymnastic rings work the same way.
Bend the knees, feet flat, to take some of the load.
regressions: Stand more upright (feet further from the anchor).
progressions: Walk the feet toward the anchor so the body is lower.

muscleNotes.lats_r: Prime mover: pulls the upper arm back past the trunk.
muscleNotes.lats_l: Prime mover: pulls the upper arm back past the trunk.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Prime mover: draws the shoulder blade back at the finish.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Prime mover: draws the shoulder blade back at the finish.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Helps pull the upper arm back.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_l: Helps pull the upper arm back.
muscleNotes.biceps_r: Bends the elbow as the bar comes in.
muscleNotes.biceps_l: Bends the elbow as the bar comes in.
muscleNotes.core: Braces the trunk so the cable does not pull it forward.
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Keep the hips extended in line with the body (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Keep the hips extended in line with the body (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Steadies the shoulder girdle; should not shrug.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Steadies the shoulder girdle; should not shrug.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Hold the hips up with the glutes so the body stays straight (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Hold the hips up with the glutes so the body stays straight (clinical opinion).
